question: What is the primary global viral cause of cardiac inflammation?
explanation: Enteroviruses, specifically coxsackieviruses, are widely recognized as the leading viral pathogens responsible for initiating cardiac tissue inflammation. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why is identifying the specific anatomical layer affected by inflammation clinically vital?

options.A: It determines whether surgical intervention will be required within twenty-four hours
options.B: It eliminates the need for any subsequent diagnostic laboratory investigations
options.C: It dictates the unique pathological process and resulting hemodynamic consequences
options.D: It guarantees the exact duration of hospital stay for the affected individual

explanation: Each heart layer responds differently to inflammation, leading to distinct mechanical and electrical complications that guide targeted therapeutic approaches. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which physical examination finding is considered a hallmark sign of acute pericarditis?
explanation: The abrasive rubbing of inflamed visceral and parietal pericardial layers produces a characteristic scratchy sound known as a pericardial friction rub. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h2)

question: A patient with acute pericarditis reports that their chest pain changes throughout the day. Which position is most likely to provide relief?

options.A: Raising both arms above the head
options.B: Lying flat in a supine position
options.C: Reclining on the left lateral side

explanation: Leaning forward pulls the heart away from the parietal pleura and the sensitive pericardial layers, reducing friction and lessening the sharp retrosternal pain. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h2)

question: What is considered the definitive gold standard diagnostic test for confirming myocarditis?
explanation: Tissue examination via endomyocardial biopsy provides direct histological confirmation of inflammatory infiltrates and myocyte necrosis, making it the definitive diagnostic standard. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h3)

question: What pathological outcome is frequently associated with the late remodeling phase of severe myocarditis?
explanation: Chronic inflammation and subsequent healing through fibrosis weaken and stretch the myocardial wall, frequently evolving into dilated cardiomyopathy with reduced ejection fraction. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h3)

question: Which specific patient population is most commonly associated with isolated tricuspid valve infective endocarditis?
explanation: Unsterile intravenous injections introduce skin flora directly into the venous system, which travels straight to the right side of the heart, preferentially infecting the tricuspid valve. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h4)

question: How do vegetations initially form on heart valves prior to microbial colonization?

options.A: Circulating white blood cells aggregate directly on normal, undamaged endothelial tissue
options.B: Myocardial muscle fibers rupture and protrude into the valvular opening
options.C: Endothelial damage causes platelet and fibrin deposition to create sterile clots
options.D: Calcium deposits progressively build up due to chronic systemic hypertension

explanation: Blood turbulence damages the endothelium, attracting platelets and fibrin to form a non-bacterial thrombotic vegetation that easily traps circulating bacteria. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary medication adjunct paired with NSAIDs to prevent the recurrence of pericarditis?
explanation: Colchicine acts as an anti-inflammatory agent that significantly lowers recurrence rates and shortens the disease course when combined with standard NSAID therapy. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h5)

question: A patient with suspected infective endocarditis is scheduled for blood cultures and intravenous antibiotic therapy. What is the correct sequence of actions?

options.A: Perform an echocardiogram before drawing any blood or giving medications
options.B: Draw blood cultures first, then administer the prescribed antibiotics
options.C: Wait for fever to spike before drawing cultures or starting medications
options.D: Administer the loading dose of antibiotics immediately, then draw cultures next day

explanation: Blood cultures must always be obtained prior to starting antimicrobial therapy to ensure the causative organism can be successfully isolated and identified. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why is strict physical rest strictly enforced during the acute phase of myocarditis?

options.A: Activity directly interferes with the diagnostic accuracy of echocardiograms
options.B: Immobility is required to allow intravenous antibiotics to reach peak serum levels
options.C: Rest prevents the formation of permanent skin lesions on the extremities
options.D: Physical exertion increases myocardial oxygen demand and can worsen tissue injury

explanation: Resting the heart minimizes workload and oxygen consumption, reducing ongoing cellular stress and the risk of fatal arrhythmias in inflamed muscle tissue. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which nursing assessment is most critical for evaluating fluid balance in a patient with acute heart failure secondary to myocarditis?
explanation: Daily weight is the most sensitive and reliable clinical indicator of acute fluid retention or loss in patients experiencing heart failure exacerbations. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is the emergency medical procedure performed to relieve cardiac tamponade by draining fluid from the pericardial space?
explanation: Pericardiocentesis involves aspirating accumulated fluid from the pericardial cavity using a needle or catheter to relieve pressure on the heart chambers. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h7)

question: What primary mechanism causes sudden hemodynamic collapse in cardiac tamponade?

options.A: Rupture of the interventricular septum allows oxygenated and deoxygenated blood to mix
options.B: External compression of the heart chambers prevents adequate diastolic ventricular filling
options.C: Severe systemic vasoconstriction causes an abrupt, uncontrollable spike in afterload
options.D: Massive electrical block stops the normal conduction system in the atria

explanation: Fluid buildup within the rigid pericardial sac exerts high pressure on the heart, preventing chambers from relaxing and filling properly during diastole. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h7)

question: What is the primary public health objective of treating streptococcal pharyngitis promptly with penicillin in young people?

options.A: Preventing acute rheumatic fever and subsequent chronic cardiac valvular damage
options.B: Stopping the transmission of viral myocarditis across school classrooms
options.C: Eliminating the risk of developing sudden idiopathic pericardial effusion
options.D: Reducing the long-term incidence of primary essential arterial hypertension

explanation: Prompt antibiotic treatment of streptococcal throat infections eradicates the bacteria and prevents the autoimmune reaction that causes rheumatic fever and heart valve destruction. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h8)

question: A patient treated for infective endocarditis is preparing for discharge. Which instruction should the nurse prioritize regarding their future health maintenance?

options.A: Avoid all forms of physical movement for the remainder of their natural life
options.B: Maintain meticulous dental hygiene and discuss antibiotic prophylaxis before invasive dental procedures
options.C: Stop taking all prescribed cardiac medications once the fever subsides completely
options.D: Restrict fluid intake completely to prevent any future episodes of peripheral edema

explanation: Poor dental hygiene allows oral bacteria to enter the bloodstream during dental procedures, seeding damaged heart valves and causing recurrent infective endocarditis. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h8)
